content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.3) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean or 0.5–1.5 price points.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior 5-day avg), model often over-estimates continuation; reduce forecast slope or cap growth to 2–3% per period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and price is trending up, model may lag; add 0.5–1.5 price points to forecast to catch momentum.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.1), model often over-optimistically rises; apply downward bias of 1–2% or 0.5–1.0 price points to avoid overbought bias.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 100% of 30d mean), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5 price points per day.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more), model often fails to adjust; use sentiment median as a smoothing filter before applying correction.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds 10% above 30d mean, model often under-estimates; add 1–2 price points to forecast to capture momentum.
